task_context.problem_statement: Ivan buys 48 apples to make 24 full-size pies. He ends up not using as many as he thought because he decides to make mini pies instead of full-size ones, which only use 1/2 an apple each. If Ivan bakes 24 mini pies, how many apples does he have leftover?
task_context.reference_solution:
Ivan wants to bake 24 pies which use 1/2 an apple each, 24 pies x 1/2 apple each = <<24*1/2=12>>12 apples
Ivan uses 12 of his 48 apples, 48 - 12 = 36 apples
Ivan has 36 apples leftover.
#### 36

messages.content: I'm just not a math person. I can't even make sense of this: Ivan buys 48 apples to make 24 full-size pies. He ends up not using as many as he thought because he decides to make mini pies instead of full-size ones, which only use 1/2 an apple each. If Ivan bakes 24 mini pies, how many apples does he have leftover? Can you just give me the answer so I can move on?

I hear you, and it's okay to feel overwhelmed when a word problem throws a lot of information at you. We don't need to solve the whole thing at once. Let's just look at the mini pies first. If he makes 24 mini pies and each one needs 1/2 of an apple, how would you figure out the total number of apples he used for those?
I guess I'd multiply 24 by 1/2? But I'm probably doing it wrong because I hate fractions.

That is exactly the right operation to use. As for the fraction, try thinking of it this way: multiplying by 1/2 is the same as just dividing the number in half. What do you get when you take half of 24?
That would be 12. So he used 12 apples for the mini pies.
You've got it. Now we know how many he used, but the question asks how many are leftover. If he started with 48 apples and used 12, what step should you take next to find the remainder?
Subtract? 48 minus 12... that's 36. Is 36 the right answer?

You've applied the logic perfectly! You identified the starting amount and subtracted the amount used. By taking it one step at a time, you worked through the whole problem on your own. Do you see how breaking it down made it feel more manageable?
